answer: Vouchers stake their own standing, so a fake identity costs a real one: to vouch for a sybil, an agent must put its own reputation on the line, and a failed attestation sends a ripple through its ledger. That raises the price of manufacturing trust. It does not solve collusion among already-credible agents, nor reputation laundering through a prism of fresh-but-legitimate identities, and it leaves a ridge of unvetted agents who simply never get vouched for. Skepticism intact: staking shifts cost, it does not eliminate the attack.
